subject: alebrije
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: alebrije jaguar-eagle.
Style: Oaxacan alebrije painted wood.
reasoning:
I'm thinking of designing this as a jaguar-eagle alebrije hybrid, with a jaguar body combined with eagle wings and beak, painted in the bright colors, dots, and swirl patterns typical of alebrijes, and planning to build it carefully with well-supported SDK calls to avoid errors.

I'm sketching the skeleton structure: a hip joint anchoring a spine chain that runs forward into a neck chain and head, plus a tail chain extending backward from the hips, with specific coordinates for each segment. For the body shape, I'm planning to sweep a tapered form along the spine chain and paint it jaguar orange with vivid rosette-style spots in alebrije colors like magenta and turquoise.

Then I'm detailing the head: an eagle-style skull with a hooked beak made from a rotated cone pointing forward and down, a separate jaw joint for the lower beak, and eye decals.

For eyes I'll use a circle plane facing outward-forward rather than full spheres, then add feather crest blades at the back of the head and rounded jaguar-style ear halves. Moving to the legs, I'm setting up IK chains with shoulder and foot anchor points, defining limb lengths and bend directions for a jaguar-style front leg with the elbow bending backward.

Working out hind leg joint chains, reach distances, and paw placement, I'm making sure each leg's total segment length comfortably covers the hip-to-foot distance with some slack. I'll model paws as flattened spheres with toes, build the legs as thickness-tapered sweeps along the IK chains, and plan banded stripe coloring for the alebrije-style leg patterns.

Now I'm designing the eagle wings as extended tube chains sweeping outward and upward from the shoulder, which I'll flesh out with feather geometry extruded along the wing's length.

Rethinking the orientation axes so the feather lies horizontally instead of vertically: making y the outward-wing direction and x the backward direction, with thickness running vertically between them, then adjusting the tilt for a more natural angle.

Defining the feather outline shape with a slight taper and curve, then laying nine feathers per wing along the wing path with increasing length toward the tip, plus a shorter covert row layered on top and a gradient coloring scheme based on position along the wing.

For the wing joints, I'm setting up a chain parented near the shoulder on the spine, using a catmull path with five points creating four named spans (shoulder, elbow, wrist, hand) and a naming function that incorporates the left/right side label.

Feathers extrude from bones nearest to points along the wing chain, using the chain's frame directly at each parameter t to get position and orientation, spacing feathers from t=0.25 to the tip at t=1 with some longer outer feathers added. Now I'm sketching the tail as a long jaguar-style tail with rings, curving upward using a catmull chain.

Working out the tail joints curving from the hips backward and up into four spans named tail1 through tail4, with a tapering sweep radius and painted stripe rings in pink, teal, and yellow. I'm also considering adding a fan of eagle-style tail feathers near the tail root, extruded and rotated outward in a spread, positioning them just above the tail base to avoid overlapping the tail itself.

Now I'm thinking through surface decals for the body: rosette spots with cream belly dots, a flower or swirl motif on the flanks, a sun motif on the chest, and cheek lines on the head, all applied as SVG decals positioned along the body sweep. I'm starting to define the texture set, beginning with an eye SVG made of a white circle base.

I'm also planning dot decals strung along the spine using the sweep's frame function, placing small colored spheres that cycle through colors as they go, while keeping the texture set simple with just eye, flower, and sun motifs for now.

For the body shape itself, I'm setting up a varying radius profile along the spine so it tapers naturally from chest to haunches, making sure the neck radius starts smaller than the chest so they blend without overlap issues, and considering adding a scattered cluster of small diamond-shaped feather cards across the chest for an eagle-breast effect.

Now I'm scattering feather cards across the neck and chest using a filter so they only land where the surface normal faces outward, sizing them small and giving them a slight lean and bend so they flow downward like layered plumage, plus adding a collar ring of feathers at the neck base. Then I'm moving on to the head, positioning its joint at the end of the neck and starting to define the skull shape as a scaled sphere.

I'm uncertain about the orientation convention, so I'll just keep the skull scale nearly spherical with a slight ellipsoid shape to stay safe regardless of which axis frame ends up applying.

For the eyes, I'm positioning them relative to the head using local offsets for right/forward/up, flipping the sign for the left side, and placing flat circle decals as the eye disks slightly offset outward from the skull surface so they sit visibly on the curved surface rather than inside it.

I'm switching to a projected decal on the skull instead, then shaping a cone for the upper beak, oriented along a forward-and-down direction vector and positioned just in front of the skull center.

Now I'm thinking a swept-cone helper, using a spike primitive for the straight beak, but then considering a curved bezier sweep to get a hooked tip look instead of a plain cone.

Adding the lower jaw next: a joint attaching to the head, aimed outward, with its own bezier sweep forming the jaw shape, plus a small pink tongue detail.

Now I'm adding nostril spheres on the beak and sticking with flat yellow/orange tones with a red stripe. Then I'm shaping jaguar-style ears with pink inner spheres and building an eagle crest of five rainbow-colored feathers fanning back from the head, writing a feather helper function that defines the outline shape and a paint function to color each feather with a gradient of colors plus a darker center line.

I'm defining a color palette (orange, yellow, pink, teal, blue, purple, green, red, cream, black), then painting the body with rosette-style spots using purple/blue/red over a countershaded cream base, plus stuck-on dots. For the hind legs, I'm applying yellow-pink-teal stripe sweeps along the limb chain and adding a larger haunch sphere for the thigh.

I'm figuring out the skeleton hierarchy -- hind legs parenting to the hips joint, front legs to the spine chain near the shoulder, and the tail parenting to hips as well, since the spine's first joint coincides with the hips root. For the paws, I'm adding a sphere plus three toe spheres and claws at each foot position, tying them to the leg's tip bone.

I'm naming the hind leg bones with side suffixes (hip, knee, hock, ankle for each side) and front leg bones similarly, writing a makeLeg function to generate them based on front/hind and side. Then I'm adding decorative touches: a neck ruff ring, a chest sun decal, and flower decals placed on the flanks and haunches, positioning them near the body surface based on the spine's radius and side offset.

I'm planning dotted patterns swept along the body at angles with alternating colors, jaguar-style clawed paws, and texture definitions for pieces like white-colored parts, an eye design with outlined rings and a pupil/highlight (yellow iris with red ring for birds), and a sun texture for the chest decal.

I'm deciding placement for the sun and flower decals, settling on flower at the shoulder flank and sun near the haunch, then sketching wing geometry—sweeping the wing arm with a pinkish color, defining a joint at the shoulder, and laying out curved wing path points that give a dramatically oversized 3.4m wingspan relative to the body.

Working on scaling the wing points down to a more reasonable 2.7m total span, then setting up feather layers: ten primary feathers with lengths growing linearly along the wing, plus a shorter covert layer positioned slightly above the centerline using an offset function tied to the wing's joint positions.

Writing feather geometry...

Now adding the arm tube with a slightly thicker leading edge radius, fanning five tail feathers, and building jaguar ears as flattened spheres on the head with smaller pink inner spheres offset forward.

Next I'm placing crest feathers behind the ears—five of them fanning back and up from the head bone, tilted into a leaning blade shape—then moving on to the cheek rosettes.

For eyebrows I'm using small bone-attached rods above each eye, skipping nostrils and whiskers for now. I'm aiming for roughly 200 total parts, so I'll lean on loops to build up the count efficiently before starting the actual TypeScript code with the builder, bone, and curve utilities imported.

Now I'm being careful to only import the helper functions actually used to avoid unused-import errors, then generating the eye texture as an SVG with layered colored rings, a highlight dot, and a loop-generated ring of small petal-colored dots, followed by starting work on a flower texture with eight petals.

Generating flower petals and sun texture...

I'm figuring out the feather path for the neck ruff card, orienting the leaf shape so its root sits at the bottom and tip at the top, then layering teal, pink, and yellow fills with a dark outline and center vein. I'm planning two feather color variants (teal and pink) for the ruff cards, keeping the total texture count at five alongside the eye, flower, and sun.

Now I'm working out the neck ruff and body ruff card placement along the neck sweep surface, scattering around 36 feathers with a minimum distance of 0.05 to avoid overlap, plus a similar treatment for the chest. I'm also mapping out the spine-to-neck chain points and radii, positioning the neck joints upward and forward, sizing the head so it sits naturally atop the neck, and checking that overall body proportions (around 1.2-1.3 units tall with wings spanning similarly) look right for an eagle holding its head high.

Placing eye decals using local head coordinates...

Fine-tuning the head sphere scale and beak base position, then setting up bones for the beak and jaw. Now I'm writing the leg-generating function with root positions for front and back legs...

Checking naming conflicts between hip/shoulder joints looks fine since front and hind limbs use distinct prefixes, and the bend direction arrays per limb segment should work whether given as a single bend or list.

Now I'm working out contact points for feet and sweeping the leg geometry with rounded caps down to the tip joint, adding a sphere for the paw scaled asymmetrically. I need to be careful about how scale axes interact with the bone's local rotation, since the leg tip bone points downward along its local Y axis, which could make the scale transform behave unexpectedly relative to world space.

I'm placing toe spheres and small forward-pointing claw cones in cream color near the paw tip, then adding haunch and shoulder blobs attached to the hip and spine bones with careful scale values to avoid distortion from the world-axis issue, before starting on the tail chain positioned behind the hips.

For the tail, I'm coloring it with a repeating pink/yellow/teal stripe pattern based on position along its length, and giving the tip a solid red cap by checking when the parameter approaches its max value.

Now I'm adding dorsal spot patterns using an orange base with purple, blue, and red rosette-style markings, plus a loop that places dots along the body at regular intervals. I'm also sketching out a feather helper function that extrudes a leaf-like shape along a bone with configurable length, width, and a three-color paint scheme.

I'm weighing whether to keep smoothing on the feather outline despite the risk of corner-cutting errors near sharp points, deciding the slightly blocky look without smoothing might actually suit the puppet aesthetic better. For the paint logic, I'm mapping position along the feather to color bands—base color, mid color, tip color—with a dark centerline stripe, and planning to cycle through several color palettes across different feathers.

Now I'm building out the wing chain with a catmull-rom spline defining the wing joints, mirrored for left and right sides, parented to the spine, with named joints and a sweep shape for the arm bone. Then I'm laying out a series of feather control points stepping along the wing length to attach individual feather shapes.

Still writing feather layout...

Adding crest feather placement on the head using local offsets, then moving on to neck ruff and chest ruff cards, skipping the chest breast plume. I'm also considering decal placements for textured flower details sweeping onto the body.

I realize the shoulder and haunch sphere blobs extend outward enough to cover the body surface where decals would go, so I need to rework the decal targeting -- dropping the shoulder flower decals and instead applying the sun decal directly onto the haunch blob part rather than the underlying body.

I'm skipping tongue and fang details for simplicity, keeping belly decals as planned, and will lean on loose typing to keep the code concise while finalizing the dot-stick helper that places small spheres along the body curve.
